chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Zur'ah ibn Muhammad, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man has zakat due from him, and he has needy relatives who are not familiar (with Wilayah). Can he give them from the zakat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, and there is no prestige. He should not make the zakat a preservation for his wealth. He can give them from other than the zakat if he wishes.'
ai.seo_question: Can a man give his zakat to his needy relatives who are not familiar with Wilayah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while relatives are preferred for zakat, those who are 'not familiar' (often interpreted in Shia scholarship as lacking knowledge of Wilayah or not being of the specific lineage required for certain zakat distributions) are excluded from receiving it directly. The Imam instructs the giver to provide for them from their own wealth (non-zakat funds) to maintain familial bonds and avoid the potential pitfall of using zakat merely as a financial shield to preserve one's own assets.
